item.description: Texans' HC announces bad news on David Montgomery for Week 9 vs. Chargers originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Houston Texans are coming out of their Week 8 bye with a poor 2-5 record, looking for a win in Week 9 against the winless Los Angeles Chargers . While there should be plenty of belief in the Texans to beat the Chargers this week, they did get some bad news about their number one running back, David Montgomery. According to Aaron Wilson of KPRC2 Houston , Texans' head coach DeMeco Ryans told reporters that Montgomery would be out for another week, though he made some progress that bodes well for a return in the near future. Texans announce bad David Montgomery news amid groin injury "Texans coach DeMeco Ryans said David Montgomery (groin) will still be out, week to week, and has made 'progress,'" Wilson reports. While Montgomery is going to miss Week 9, and his status going forward will continue to be up in the air, it's good to hear that he's making progress. Coming out of the Texans' Week 8 bye, backup running back Woody Marks will be the lead back going forward. He's shown some flashes since taking over, and he'll face a leaky Chargers defense with a chance to further prove his worth this season. Montgomery meanwhile will miss another game, making it his third game he's missed with this groin injury he suffered against the Tennessee Titans back in Week 5. MORE : Why it's time for Colts to move on from Shane Steichen and Daniel Jones This update from Ryans does point to Montgomery getting closer to a return, and considering the Texans didn't place him on injured reserve, a Week 10 return would seemingly be in play. With Montgomery being ruled out for Week 9, he'll have missed four weeks due to this injury, but only three total games. Week 10 is in play, but even if he misses that game, a Week 11 return against the Indianapolis Colts would be welcomed. The Texans, at 2-5, are running out of time to contend for a playoff spot and the AFC South. Getting healthy, including getting Montgomery back, would help. But that's going to have to wait a week, as he's been ruled out for Week 9. item.description: Tiger Woods celebrates after making a putt on the 18th green to win The Masters golf tournament at Augusta National Golf Club on April 14, 2019. Next season, Tiger Woods is seriously considering competing on the PGA Tour Champions . The 50-year-old legend wants to compete against other veterans who know his game. This move could change the entire landscape of senior golf forever. Two-time season champion Steven Alker says the talk in the locker room is that Woods is ready to return. He wants to win big events, especially the US Senior Open. Winning that one trophy would let Woods move ahead of Bobby Jones. Woods and Bobby Jones are tied at nine USGA national championships. A U.S. Senior Open victory would give Woods his tenth and put him ahead of Jones. Alker told reporters at a Phoenix Country Club media day that Woods is serious about this plan. The 15-time major champion has been limited by injuries in recent years. The senior circuit offers a different challenge with golf carts and shorter rounds. This setup gives Woods a much better chance to win tournaments again. The Real Hurdle Is Not The Body Woods is not the only topic on the minds of senior players. A huge split has formed over whether LIV Golf veterans should be allowed back on tour. The current season ends next week with the Charles Schwab Cup Championship. But the 2027 campaign is already causing heated debates among the membership. Some players want recognizable names to bring more eyes and money to the tour. Others refuse to welcome golfers who left for lucrative contracts elsewhere. Alker called the situation a “Catch-22” during his media session. “We want players to keep the profile of the tour up,” Alker said, according to Yahoo Sports . “And then you got guys on the tour who don’t want those guys at all.” He admitted that the Player Advisory Council has discussed this issue extensively. The tour’s membership remains divided over whether returning LIV players should face the same suspension rules as other golfers. The tour needs to decide if past choices matter more than future revenue. Friends Want Him, But The Tour Fights Woods has friends on the circuit who really want him to play their events. Steve Stricker and Jim Furyk host invitationals that would fit his schedule perfectly. item.description: Pat McAfee is a problem for ESPN’s “College GameDay,” Joe Scarborough of “Morning Joe” hammered away at Tuesday during election day. item.title: What Brian Windhorst thought about Draymond Green’s ‘face of the franchise’ comment on Yaxel Lendeborg
item.description: Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images Draymond Green kept his Michigan rivalry aside and took rookie Yaxel Lendeborg under his wing when the Golden State Warriors drafted the former Wolverines player 11th overall in the draft. Just eight games into the season, he has shown why he was one of the leaders on the team that won the national championship last year. The 24-year-old is averaging 21.5 points and 7 rebounds on 50% shooting from the field. After preseason, it was clear that Lendeborg was going to play a big role for the team. Coach Steve Kerr had nothing but praise for him but Draymond Green took things a notch higher. “The Golden State Warriors have found the next face of the franchise,” Green said, while heaping praise on the rookie. Brian Windhorst was shocked by Draymond Green’s praise of Yaxel Lendeborg On his podcast, Green is very vocal about players and does not shy away from going off if they make mistakes. For someone so critical of the game, Brian Windhorst was shocked to hear the comments from Green, which gave him a sense of the player Lendeborg was. “I’m not making like a blanket statement here but like Draymond is not afraid to criticise people, he doesn’t hand out praise like that. When he said that, I sat up, ‘Seriously?’ I do think he’s a lot in terms of like managing and I think Kerr has the temperament, I do think he needed a team that could manage all of the aspects of him, that team found him,” said Windhorst on The Hoops Collective Podcast. He showed a glimpse of how he can manage the challenge of leading a team in the most recent game against the Los Angeles Clippers. The 24-year-old scored 37 points on 13-for-19 shooting from the field, which proves that he can score efficiently, a quality vital in the NBA. While his scoring has been elite, Lendeborg would want to reduce the number of turnovers he has conceded. In eight games, the 24-year-old has given up 3.4 turnovers per game. The Warriors have won five games since starting the season 0-3. During this run, Lendeborg has averaged 23.2 points and 6.2 rebounds for the Dubs. This indicates that he is integral to their success and if they are to make a deep playoff run, the Warriors will need their rookie to play at an All-Star level, especially with Jimmy Butler only expected to be back in February. item.title: The secret behind Miami's explosive offense? A Louisiana country boy who almost walked away from football
item.description: CORAL GABLES, Fla. — The wallpaper of Shannon Dawson's office is a tapestry of a football coach's first language: Xs and Os. Scribbled in black marker, scrawled across three of four walls in the Miami offensive coordinator's digs are play designs, route concepts and offensive formations. You can barely make them out. A film junkie, Dawson's office is often dimly lit as a television glows from across the room. But as the lights flicker on, the walls come alive. There's a surprise here too: a fourth wall — a window looking out to the team's indoor practice facility — is also covered in play designs. Window or wall, no surface can escape Dawson's felted weapon. "We call it 'The Think Tank,'" Dawson says of the window, which, unlike the three walls, holds concepts to be used at a later date instead of the current game week. A country boy at heart, his accent dripping with those south Louisiana and Mississippi roots, the 49-year-old Dawson helps steer the nation's most explosive offense for the country's top-ranked team. Miami deploys college football's most efficient and productive quarterback (Darian Mensah completes 80% of his passes and throws for the sixth-most yards in the sport); its most electrifying receiver (Malachi Toney has caught the second-most touchdowns); and two bruising backs (Mark Fletcher and Javian Mallory combine for 16 scores). As the unbeaten Hurricanes barrel toward perhaps the most anticipated regular game in college football this year — No. 1 Miami vs. No. 11 Notre Dame in South Bend — Dawson's unit is humming at a breakneck pace: no team averages more points a game (46.7); no one has gained more first downs (224); and only one other program gains more yards per snap (7.7). How? The short answer is that coach Mario Cristobal has stockpiled talent; created a hotly competitive team environment; developed athletes into fierce football players; and, four years ago, took a giant leap: He hired Houston's offensive coordinator, then a somewhat unknown disciple of the Air Raid offense who, in his biggest job (Kentucky in 2015) lasted one season. You can find that someone within that dimly lit room, his language sprinkled across wall and window, a man who's blended the pass-heavy concepts of Hal Mumme and Mike Leach with Cristobal's intensely physical running game to produce something altogether scary for opposing defenses. "Adapt or die," Cristobal says from his office on hiring Dawson, perhaps not dissimilar to Nick Saban plucking Lane Kiffin in 2014 to reinvent his offense. "Shannon has been able to morph the principles of the Air Raid with the power running game and screen game. He feels like we're just starting to hit our stride." item.description: Christian Pulisic and Folarin Balogun sustained injuries during the World Cup (Dean Mouhtaropoulos) United States coach Mauricio Pochettino on Wednesday recalled Christian Pulisic and Folarin Balogun alongside several promising young stars in his squad for the upcoming CONCACAF Nations League quarter-finals against Haiti. Neither Pulisic nor Balogun have played for the US since suffering injuries at this summer's World Cup and subsequently missed the start of their club seasons with AC Milan and Monaco respectively. Pulisic fractured his leg during the United States' round-of-16 World Cup loss to Belgium. "Happy to see again Balo because I think after the World Cup, we have the possibility to see, and it is a great opportunity for him to keep improving in his confidence." For the clashes with Haiti on November 14 and 17, the national team mainstays will be joined by a raft of youngsters including Justin Ellis, 19, and Julian Hall, 18. Both made their debuts and scored during the United States' international window in September and October, in which Pochettino's youthful roster won all four games against Peru, Chile, Mexico and Canada. "I think it's a great opportunity for different players now, and for a different roster than was in the last camp, to have the possibility to mix younger with experienced players," said Pochettino. The 'away' leg of the quarter-finals will take place in Miami, Florida on November 14, followed by the home leg three days later in Cincinnati, Ohio. item.title: Mike Vrabel addresses Patriots rumors ahead of NFL trade deadline
item.description: A pair of New England Patriots veterans found themselves in trade rumors ahead of the NFL’s trade deadline . This week, defensive tackle Christian Barmore and cornerback Carlton Davis were mentioned as potential trade candidates by Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer. According to Breer, trading either player would give New England an opportunity to add needed draft capital while getting younger. Speaking on Wednesday, head coach Mike Vrabel responded to the report. “I think sometimes national reports have the tendency to do that. I have not shared that information with anybody,” Vrabel said. “You know, this time of year, I think that all these things kind of get drummed up. So we’re focused on trying to prepare for Green Bay, make the corrections from the game. I mean, this is business as normal here. So, I don’t know where a lot of these things come from. Certainly not any conversations with me.” Davis, 29, has played in four games this season while dealing with a neck injury. When healthy, he has occupied his usual starting role opposite Christian Gonzalez, with Vrabel highlighting his physicality and competitiveness. Barmore, 27, has seen his playing time decrease slightly, playing just 50% of New England’s defensive snaps this season after logging 65% last year. The defensive tackle has been productive at times, recording 3.5 sacks, his highest total since 2023. Neither player has guaranteed money remaining on his contract beyond this season, making a potential trade a realistic possibility. However, would dealing away two defensive contributors make sense for a 5-3 Patriots team with aspirations of competing? “I don’t know. There’s probably a bunch of ways we can make this team better,” Vrabel responded. “You know, coach better, execute better, whether that’s [adding] guys on the streets or — there’s multiple ways. Again, we’d have these conversations each and every day.” Vrabel said he doesn’t feel the need to discuss trade rumors with players, instead keeping conversations centered on football and the team’s preparation. The NFL trade deadline is set for Tuesday, Nov. 10, at 4 p.m. ET.
